tier_reason: A stands: public benchmark code, toolchain and CPU; the baseline difference is a same-task idiom difference, documented.

corrections.caveats: Enricher: the fast-sp rust_iter baseline sums into isize, so the autovectorised loop gets only 2 lanes per 128-bit register, while the SIMD version reduces in i8 lanes per 16 bytes; part of the 5.0x is that accumulator width. The README table comes from 2023 code and was not rerun after the 2026-07-30 changes. Gotchas: float reduce_sum is ordered (sequential) and float reduce_max/reduce_min are a scalar fold; Simd values pass through memory unless inlined; swizzle_dyn's fast path needs std rebuilt (-Zbuild-std); issue #297 finds u64/i64 SIMD sums no faster than an autovectorised loop; stabilisation is still blocked (issue #364, PRs #493 and #483, August 2026).

corrections.maintenance_status: abandoned (archived 2026-09-16; final release 0.3.9 on 2023-07-30; does not build on nightlies since 1.78.0-nightly, 2024-03-02)
corrections.caveats: Enricher: the ispc_tasks baseline runs on ispc-rs's own Rust task system (it spawns num_cpus threads on first launch and the syncing thread sleeps 50 ms when no chunk is left; checked in ispc-rs 1.0.11 and HEAD, the 2018 version was not fetchable), a plausible cause of stencil ispc_tasks being slower than serial ispc on both Xeons (395 vs 287 ms, 401 vs 185 ms), so the headline wins over ISPC are against a weak task runtime. hyperfine timing includes process start, thread-pool creation and aobench's PNG write; aobench also prints an internal kernel-only timer and the readmes do not say which number the tables use. 0.3.9 no longer builds on current nightly (platform_intrinsics feature removed, issue #360); the only reported workaround is pinning a 1.77-era nightly. Interim crate name packed_simd_2 (0.3.4-0.3.8).
